nginxions.traffic.top.origins.info.defaultMessage: The addresses of your servers (upstreams) nginx sent requests to.

nginxions.traffic.top.paths-bytes.info.defaultMessage: The paths that sent the most data: large files, video, backups.

nginxions.traffic.top.protocols.info.defaultMessage: Versions of HTTP the clients used.

nginxions.traffic.top.referers.info.defaultMessage: The sites people came from by a link (the Referer header). Direct visits are not here.

nginxions.traffic.top.slow-paths.info.defaultMessage: The paths your servers answer slowest (p95 of the answer time).

nginxions.traffic.top.tls.info.defaultMessage: Versions of TLS of the HTTPS connections. Old versions (1.0, 1.1) mean old clients or scanners.

nginxions.traffic.top.uncached-paths.inf.defaultMessage: The paths that went to your server past the cache most often: candidates to cache.

nginxions.traffic.top.uncached-types.inf.defaultMessage: Types of content that went past the cache.

nginxions.traffic.unknown-hosts.text.defaultMessage: {hosts} point to this server but are not in Hosts: the default site answers them. Add them as hosts, or let the default site drop them (444).

nginxions.traffic.unknown-hosts.title.defaultMessage: {count} requests to domains that are not in Hosts

nginxions.traffic.unknown-hosts.title.in.defaultMessage: Requests to domains that are not in Hosts: they are answered by the default page. Usually scanners walking addresses, or a DNS record pointing here by mistake.

nginxions.traffic.unsupported.defaultMessage: Traffic analytics needs PostgreSQL (the database of the NginxionS stack).

nginxions.traffic.visitors.hint.defaultMessage: Page views and visits are of people. A page view is an HTML page answered without an error; a visit is a page view that did not come from the same site. Bots say who they are (search engines, previews, monitoring, scripts) or pose as a browser without its headers; scanners probe for files and admin pages, come to the bare IP or are refused by the protection. The charts split them: click the legend to pick out one.

nginxions.traffic.visits-over-time.info.defaultMessage: Visits in each interval, split into people, bots and scanners.

nginxions.user.password-hint.defaultMessage: At least 8 characters. The user can change it later in their profile.

nginxions.users.search.defaultMessage: Search by name, nickname or email

nginxions.waf.agent-settings.fail-open.o.defaultMessage: Fail-close: if the agent does not answer in time or is down, requests to protected hosts are rejected (security first).
If the agent does not answer in time or is down, nginx lets the request through without inspection (availability first).

nginxions.waf.agent-settings.pending.defaultMessage: Saved settings are not applied yet: the agent has not restarted since.

nginxions.waf.agent-settings.restart-war.defaultMessage: The agent restarts to apply the settings (a few seconds). With fail-open on, traffic keeps flowing without inspection meanwhile; with fail-close, requests to protected hosts are rejected until the agent is back.

nginxions.waf.agent-settings.saved.defaultMessage: Settings saved, the agent is restarting

nginxions.waf.agent-unreachable.defaultMessage: The agent is not reachable. Check the openappsec service in Overview → Services.

nginxions.waf.events.action.info.defaultMessage: What the protection did: blocked (the request did not reach your server), detected (it passed and was only recorded), a ban or captcha of CrowdSec.

nginxions.waf.events.description.defaultMessage: What the agents found and reported: attacks open-appsec detected or blocked, CrowdSec alerts and the notices of the open-appsec agent; each row names its agent. mTLS refusals have their own tab; every request to the hosts is on the Requests tab.

nginxions.waf.events.event.info.defaultMessage: What happened: the type of attack or the scenario of CrowdSec, and its name.

nginxions.waf.events.host.info.defaultMessage: The domain the request was sent to.

nginxions.waf.events.request.info.defaultMessage: The method and the path of the request. Open the event to see the parameter and the sample that triggered it.

nginxions.waf.events.severity.info.defaultMessage: How dangerous the agent considers it: critical and high are attacks to look at, medium and low are suspicious, info is for the record.

nginxions.waf.events.source-ip.info.defaultMessage: The address of the client and its country by the GeoIP database. A click adds it to the filters.

nginxions.waf.events.time.info.defaultMessage: When the agent saw the event, in the time zone of your browser.

nginxions.waf.events.unavailable.defaultMessage: The agent's log directory is not readable: is the open-appsec agent running?

nginxions.waf.expert.example.defaultMessage: Example: accept traffic of a trusted IP on all protected hosts

nginxions.waf.expert.no-diff.defaultMessage: The fragment is valid, local_policy.yaml stays the same

nginxions.waf.expert.no-versions.defaultMessage: No fragments yet: the policy is generated from the WAF settings of the hosts only

nginxions.waf.expert.saved.defaultMessage: The policy was saved and sent to the agent

nginxions.waf.minimum-confidence.hint.defaultMessage: High is recommended. Lower values block more, with more false positives.

nginxions.waf.mode.detect-learn.hint.defaultMessage: Attacks are logged, nothing is blocked. The model keeps learning.

nginxions.waf.mode.prevent-learn.hint.defaultMessage: Attacks are blocked with 403 and logged. The model keeps learning.
